name: Texas Hold'em
description: Texas Hold'em is the world's most popular poker variant. Each player receives two private hole cards, and five community cards are dealt face-up on the table. Players make the best five-card poker hand using any combination of their hole cards and the community cards. The game features four rounds of betting and combines skill, strategy, and psychology.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Robstown, Texas, USA
Time Period: Early 1900s (circa 1920s)
Creator(s): Unknown (developed in Texas card rooms)
Etymology: Named after Texas, where it originated, and "Hold'em" refers to players holding their own cards while sharing community cards
timeline: 1920s-1960s: Played primarily in Texas card rooms and underground games
1967: Introduced to Las Vegas by Doyle Brunson, Amarillo Slim, and other Texas road gamblers
1970: First World Series of Poker (WSOP) Main Event was Texas Hold'em
1980s-1990s: Grew in popularity in California card rooms and Las Vegas
1998: First online poker room (Planet Poker) launched, featuring Hold'em
2003: Chris Moneymaker's WSOP win after online satellite qualification sparked the "Poker Boom"
2006: Unlawful Internet Gambling Enforcement Act (UIGEA) passed in US
2010s-Present: Global expansion, live streaming, mobile apps, and regulated online poker

rules.objective: Make the best five-card poker hand using any combination of your two hole cards and the five community cards. Win chips by having the best hand at showdown or by making all other players fold.
rules.gameplay: Blinds. Deal 2 hole cards each. Pre-flop betting. Flop (3 community cards), turn (1), river (1). Betting after each. Showdown: best 5-card hand from 7. Win by best hand or all fold.
keyRules: Blinds: small blind and big blind (or dealer/non-dealer in heads-up). Big blind equals minimum bet.
Each player receives two hole cards face down. No player may show hole cards before showdown.
Four betting rounds: pre-flop (after hole cards), after flop (3 community cards), after turn (1 card), after river (1 card).
Dealer burns one card before dealing each community round (flop, turn, river).
Best five-card poker hand from the seven available (two hole plus five board) wins. Player may use 0, 1, or 2 hole cards.
At showdown all active players must show both hole cards. Last bettor/raiser shows first; ties split the pot.

strategy.basic:
Starting Hand Selection by Position

 Position  Playable Hands 
-------------------------
 Early (UTG, UTG+1)  AA, KK, QQ, AKs, AQs 
 Middle  Add: JJ, TT, AKo, AJs, KQs, QJs 
 Late (Cutoff, Button)  Add: 99-22, ATs-A2s, KTs, suited connectors 
 Blinds  Defend with wider range due to pot odds 
Key Principles
1. Play tight in early position
2. Loosen up in late position
3. Raise more than you call
4. Fold when beat
5. Don't chase draws without odds
strategy.intermediate:
Continuation Betting
Bet flop after raising pre-flop (~60-75% of pot)
More effective on dry boards
Less effective on coordinated/wet boards
Consider opponent's range
Pot Odds and Equity
Calculate: Call amount / (Pot + Call amount)
Compare to chance of winning
Call when equity > pot odds required
Position Play
Act last = more information
Steal blinds from late position
Control pot size in position
Avoid marginal spots out of position
strategy.advanced:
Range Analysis
Think in ranges, not specific hands
Consider what hands opponent would play this way
Balance your own ranges
Use blockers to construct bluffs
Board Texture
Dry boards (rainbow, disconnected): Bluff more
Wet boards (two-tone, connected): Bet bigger for protection
Dynamic boards: Consider future streets
Static boards: Current hand strength matters more
Game Theory Optimal (GTO) vs Exploitative
GTO: Unexploitable baseline
Exploitative: Deviate to maximize profit vs mistakes
Against unknowns: Play GTO
Against known mistakes: Exploit
tips: 2. Calling too much (folding is often correct)

variations.name: Pineapple
variations.description: Each player is dealt three hole cards and must discard one before the first round of betting. Otherwise same as Texas Hold'em.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: Crazy Pineapple
variations.description: Each player is dealt three hole cards and keeps all three until after the second betting round. Each active player must discard one card immediately before the turn is dealt.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: Crazy Pineapple Hi-Lo 8 or Better
variations.description: Crazy Pineapple with pot split between highest and lowest hands. Low hand: five different ranks 8 or lower, aces low, no straights or flushes. Best low is A-2-3-4-5.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: Tahoe (Wichita Hold'em)
variations.description: Each player is dealt three hole cards and keeps all three until showdown. A player may use 0, 1 or 2 hole cards (not all three) with board cards to make their final hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: Irish
variations.description: Each player is dealt four hole cards, kept until after the second betting round. Before the turn, each active player must discard two cards, keeping two for turn and river.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: Informal (No Burn)
variations.description: Home game variant: community cards dealt face down to the table at the start; three turned up after first betting round, one after second, one after third. No burn cards.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: No Limit
variations.description: Players may bet any amount up to their full stack at any time. Most common in tournaments and cash games.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: Fixed Limit
variations.description: Bet and raise amounts are fixed (e.g. small bet preflop and flop, big bet turn and river). Typically one bet plus three or four raises per round.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: Pot Limit
variations.description: Maximum bet or raise is the current pot size. Balances no-limit and fixed-limit play.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: Heads-Up (2 Players)
variations.description: Two players only. Dealer posts small blind, non-dealer posts big blind. Action order and strategy differ from full table.

variations.name: Short-Handed (3-5 Players)
variations.description: Played with three to five players. Tighter hand requirements than full ring; position and aggression matter more.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: Full Ring (6-10 Players)
variations.description: Standard table size. Optimal with six to nine players. Tighter play than short-handed.

variations.name: Straddle
variations.description: Optional third blind (typically double the big blind) posted by the player to the left of the big blind before cards are dealt. Creates a larger pot and different action order.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

variations.name: Casino Versions
variations.description: Formal card-room and casino rules: mandatory burn before each community deal, strict betting order, and house procedures.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is rule-only; no engine overrides required for this variant.
